newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Prodi hopes to detail "Euro-tax" by Nov 9.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Prodi hopes to detail "Euro-tax" by Nov 9.

text.p: Italy's Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Thursday that he hoped to finalise details of a one-off "Euro-tax" in his 1997 draft budget by November 9.
Prodi was answering questions in the lower house of parliament about the budget, which aims to cut next year's deficit by 62.5 trillion lire ($42 billion).

Some 12 trillion lire in revenues are due to come from the special "Euro-tax". It is being proposed to help Italy make the grade for membership of Europe's planned single currency but details of how it will be raised have yet to be outlined.
The tax is included in the final part of the budget package.

"The final part of the budget itself has not been defined because we have already said that it will be defined in the coming days," Prodi told a member of parliament for the hard right National Alliance party, Maurizio Gasparri.
"I hope that on November 9 you will have all the elements you need to be able to decide on the budget calmly," he said.
